title: 3-Read Friday #51: Listening, Cold Calling, and Hinge Questions
author: Craig Barton
summary: In the fifty-first instalment of his weekly roundup, Craig Barton curates three blog posts he found interesting that week, each with his own brief editorial framing. He links Alex Quigley's case for explicitly teaching listening as a lost classroom skill, tying it to his own recent obsession with student non-listening after a conversation with Pritesh Raichura. He then flags Claudia Lewis's contrarian post arguing teachers should stop 'cold calling' and instead practise targeted questioning, praising it for challenging one of his long-standing beliefs. Finally, he highlights David Didau's piece on writing effective hinge-point multiple-choice questions in English, noting his own bias toward diagnostic questions in maths and his interest in how the same idea plays out in another subject. As usual, the newsletter closes with a plug for his back-catalogue of newsletters and a nod to the weekend.
points: Barton frames all three picks around checking what students actually understand in the moment -- through listening, targeted questioning, or hinge-point MCQs -- rather than assuming engagement equals learning.

He flags Claudia Lewis's post as valuable precisely because it challenges a belief he has held for a long time, modelling intellectual openness rather than picking only pieces that confirm his priors.
He connects Quigley's listening piece back to his own podcast conversation with Pritesh Raichura, showing how the newsletter functions as a running thread across his other work, not a one-off list.
He explicitly notes his own disciplinary bias (maths) when recommending Didau's English-specific post, modelling how a technique like hinge questions transfers across subjects.
quotes: Here are three blog posts that I found interesting this week.
Ever since my conversation with Pritesh Raichura, I have become obsessed with students listening - or more accurately, students not listening - in the classroom.
This post from Alex shares some concrete strategies we can use to help our students listen more.
I love a post that challenges one of my long-standing beliefs.
Here, Claudia addresses a fundamental issue with Cold Calling students, and suggests what we can do instead.
Regular readers will know that I am a sucker for a good multiple-choice diagnostic question.
However, my experience is largely confined to the world of maths.
Therefore, I enjoyed David’s post, delving into what makes an effective multiple-choice diagnostic question in English.
